data.narrative:
Zephyr Fusion is a pre-seed nuclear energy company founded by two plasma physics veterans with 15+ and 20+ years of experience in diagnostics and modeling, respectively, both formerly at national laboratories. The target sector comprises 10 comparable entities: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private firms including Helion, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

Valuation analysis relied on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-progression methodology, using the company's $500K in total raised as a proxy for base value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of pre-seed-to-next-stage advancement, yields an implied valuation of $1.25M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable; while 6 same-sector comparables exist, none provided sufficient overlap at the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier to support reliable benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.06M to $1.44M, with a median point of $1.25M. This reflects minimal triangulation depth—only one method is sufficiently grounded in the available data. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable pre-seed nuclear companies, the nascent stage of the venture limiting financial or operational metrics, and the reliance on stage-progression alone as the primary anchor. Investors should weight this valuation heavily toward the broad range rather than point estimates, pending additional market data or expanded comparable analysis.
